title: repo_chatbot_w1x035xk
summary: The **repo_chatbot_w1x035xk** repository contains tools and test cases for image manipulation, focusing on BMP file handling, pixel data conversion, filters (e.g., gamma correction, contrast, convolution), and memory management for kernel operations, with examples of ASCII art generation and BMP format validation.

nodes.title: README.md
nodes.text: # image_processing My lazy ass...finally decided to add a readme...lol: Anyways here is whats up... I basically tried making openCV from scratch in C... This only works on BMP file format... Cus Bitmap is damn Simple haha ya so i used only standard C libs... Extracted the DIB and BMP header info...got the shape and size of image... and also the loc in the bmp file where img data starts... Extracted the image data into an RGB struct array... and BAM! U can do any kind of crazy stuff with it...like ascii art: lol # I also implemented stuff like: # 1> convolution # 2> min and maxpooling # 3> edge detection like: sobels, DoG, etc # 4> blurring filters # 5> some morphological op like: dilation and erosion # 6> histogram equilization # 7> some basic func: like log and gamma function # 8> also fun stuff like: ascii art and "coloured" ascii art I am planning to add other stuff later... and yes ik what u might think...I could have done optimizations like sliding window/ rolling hash...yah i could... but why...Like it works good enough for now...and yah revisiting and changing stuff is annoying # AND YES I AM A ONE PIECE FAN LOL

nodes.title: image_processing
nodes.summary: The **image_processing** folder contains tools and test cases for image manipulation, including BMP file handling, pixel data conversion, and various filters. It includes utilities for validating BMP formats, applying gamma correction and contrast adjustments, performing dilation and convolution operations, and generating ASCII art representations of processed images. The folder also demonstrates memory management for kernel operations in convolutional processing.

nodes.title: bmp_img_processor.c
nodes.summary: The `bmp_img_processor.c` file contains functions for BMP image processing, including validation of file format and headers, error handling, parsing of BMP and DIB headers, loading pixel data into structured formats, and converting RGB images to grayscale. It provides utilities for checking BMP signatures, extracting metadata, and managing image data with padding and memory allocation.

nodes.title: errMsg
nodes.summary: The `errMsg` function maps error codes to descriptive messages, printing specific error details for known codes or a provided default message for unknown errors, and returns 1 on failure (non-zero `err`) or 0 on success. It handles BMP file validation errors and custom error messages via a switch-case structure.

nodes.title: isBMP
nodes.summary: The `isBMP` function checks if a file is a BMP image by reading the first two bytes and verifying they match the BMP file signature "BM". It returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise.

nodes.title: BMP_HEADER
nodes.summary: The `getBMPHeader` function reads and parses the BMP file header from a given file, validating it as a BMP and extracting key fields (`bm`, `size`, `garb`, `addr`) into a `BMP_HEADER` struct. It returns the struct on success or `NULL` on errors (e.g., file not found, invalid format, memory allocation failure).

nodes.title: DIB_HEADER
nodes.summary: The `getDIBHeader` function reads and parses the DIB header from a BMP file, extracting key metadata like dimensions, color depth, and compression settings. It opens the file, validates it as a BMP, and populates a `DIB_HEADER` struct by reading binary data from the file's specified header offset.

nodes.title: isValidFormat
nodes.summary: The `isValidFormat` function checks if a file is a valid 24-bit uncompressed BMP image by verifying its file type, header compression method, and bits per pixel, returning 1 for valid or 0 for invalid/format mismatches. It opens the file, validates BMP structure, and inspects DIB header parameters before cleaning up resources.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `getImage` function reads a BMP file, parses its headers, and loads pixel data into an `IMG` structure, handling padding and memory allocation, with output as a structured RGB array. It processes the file in reverse row order due to BMP's bottom-up storage format.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `greyScale` function converts an RGB image to grayscale by calculating each pixel's intensity using the formula `0.3*R + 0.6*G + 0.1*B`, returning a new `IMG` structure with the grayscale pixel data. It allocates memory for the output image and copies dimensions from the input.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `bwImg` function converts a color image to a black-and-white (binary) image by thresholding grayscale values. It calculates each pixel's luminance using a weighted sum (0.3R + 0.6G + 0.1B), then sets pixels to white (255) if the value ≥128, else black (0), returning a new `IMG` structure with this binary data.

nodes.title: renderAsciiArt
nodes.summary: The `renderAsciiArt` function converts an image into ASCII art by mapping each pixel's brightness (calculated via weighted RGB values) to characters from a predefined set, then writes the result to "ascii.txt". It uses a luminosity formula (0.3R + 0.6G + 0.1B) to determine character intensity and maps it to the appropriate ASCII symbol.

nodes.title: renderAsciiArt_color
nodes.summary: The `renderAsciiArt_color` function converts an image into colored ASCII art by mapping each pixel's RGB values to a character from a gradient string, using ANSI escape codes to match the pixel's color, and printing the result to stdout. It processes each pixel's intensity via a weighted average formula to select the appropriate character and applies color formatting for visual accuracy.

nodes.title: render_terminal
nodes.summary: The `render_terminal` function converts each pixel's RGB values into ANSI color codes to display an image in the terminal, printing each pixel's color followed by `<>` and a newline, then resetting the terminal color. It iterates through all pixels, applying a weighted average (unused) and directly using RGB values for terminal color formatting.

nodes.title: freeIMG
nodes.summary: The `freeIMG` function deallocates memory for an image structure by recursively freeing its 2D RGB pixel array and then the structure itself, ensuring no memory leaks. It takes an `IMG*` input and returns `void`, handling both row-wise and structural memory release.

nodes.title: createIMG
nodes.summary: The `createIMG` function generates a BMP image file by writing the BMP and DIB headers followed by pixel data, calculating row padding based on bit depth and width to ensure proper alignment. It takes a file path, image data, and header structures as inputs, outputting a valid BMP file with correctly formatted headers and padded pixel rows.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `edgeDetect_gradient` function detects edges in an image by calculating intensity gradients in three directions (horizontal, vertical, diagonal) using a threshold. It outputs a new image where pixels meeting the threshold are marked white (edges), otherwise black. Core logic involves luminance calculation, neighbor intensity comparisons, and threshold-based edge highlighting.

nodes.title: edgeRenderer
nodes.summary: The `edgeRenderer` function processes an image to visualize edges by comparing intensity differences between adjacent pixels, using a threshold to determine which directional edges (horizontal, vertical, diagonal) to highlight with symbols (`-`, `|`, `/`, `\`) or spaces. It calculates weighted intensity values and checks directional gradients to render edge patterns.

nodes.title: createImgDirect
nodes.summary: The `createImgDirect` function generates a BMP image file by initializing BMP and DIB headers, calculating padding for 24-bit RGB alignment, and writing the image data to the specified file. It takes an image structure and file path as inputs, outputting a properly formatted BMP file with metadata and pixel data.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `concatIMGX` function horizontally concatenates two images (`img1` and `img2`) with specified padding between them, allocating a new image structure and copying pixel data while aligning memory to 32-bit boundaries. It handles varying heights by padding the shorter image with the given color values (`padr`, `padg`, `padb`).

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `concatIMGY` function vertically concatenates two images (`img1` and `img2`) with specified padding between them, returning a new image. It copies pixel data from both inputs into the new image, filling padding regions with given RGB values (`padr`, `padg`, `padb`), and adjusts dimensions to accommodate the combined height and alignment requirements.

nodes.title: convolution_size
nodes.summary: The `convolution_size` function calculates the output dimension of a 1D convolution operation by applying the formula `(image_size - kernel_size) / stride + 1`, taking `image_size`, `kernel_size`, and `stride` as inputs and returning the computed output size.

nodes.title: rgbRange
nodes.summary: The `rgbRange` function clamps an integer input `val` between 0 and 255, ensuring it fits within valid RGB value bounds by returning 0 for negative inputs and 255 for values exceeding 255, otherwise returning the input directly.

nodes.title: kernelWt
nodes.summary: The `kernelWt` function calculates the sum of absolute values in a kernel matrix by iterating through each element, converting negatives to positives, and accumulating the total. It takes a `KERNEL` struct pointer as input and returns a float representing the summed absolute values.

nodes.title: kernelPosWt
nodes.summary: The `kernelPosWt` function calculates the sum of all positive values in a kernel's matrix, returning the total as a float. It iterates through each element of the matrix, adding positive values to a cumulative sum.

nodes.title: kernelNegWt
nodes.summary:
The `kernelNegWt` function calculates the sum of all negative values in a kernel's matrix. It iterates through each element, adding negative entries to a cumulative sum, which is returned as the result.  
**Input:** Pointer to a `KERNEL` struct containing a 2D matrix.  
**Output:** Floating-point sum of all negative matrix elements.  
**Core Logic:** Checks each matrix value; if negative, adds it to the total sum.

nodes.title: weighted_kernel_correction
nodes.summary:
The `weighted_kernel_correction` function adjusts RGB values by dividing each component by either the kernel's positive or negative weight (depending on the value's sign) and clamps them to a valid range, using kernel-derived weights for normalization.  
**Inputs:** RGB integers, kernel struct. **Outputs:** Corrected RGB values. **Core Logic:** Conditional division by positive/negative kernel weights followed by range clamping.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary:
The `convolution` function applies a kernel to an image via matrix multiplication, accumulating RGB values from overlapping image regions, then adjusts them using a provided correction function, outputting a new image with convolved pixel data.  
**Inputs**: Image, kernel, correction function.  
**Output**: New image with convolved pixels.  
**Core Logic**: Nested loops iterate over the image, compute weighted sums via the kernel, apply correction, and store results in a padded RGB array.

nodes.title: printKernel
nodes.summary: The `printKernel` function prints the matrix of a KERNEL struct in a formatted, row-by-row manner, using nested loops to iterate through each element and formatted output (`%.2f`) to display floating-point values with two decimal places.

nodes.title: printImgMatrix
nodes.summary: The `printImgMatrix` function prints an image's RGB pixel matrix to the terminal, using ANSI escape codes to set text color based on each pixel's RGB values and displaying their average intensity. It iterates through all pixels, outputs color-coded text, and formats the result row-by-row.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `sobelsEdgeDectorHorizontal` function applies a 3x3 Sobel kernel to detect horizontal edges in an image. It convolves the input image with a horizontally oriented Sobel filter, returning a new image highlighting edge gradients along the horizontal axis.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `sobelsEdgeDectorVertical` function applies the Sobel vertical edge detection kernel via convolution to an input image, producing a new image highlighting vertical edges. It uses a 3x3 kernel with weights [[1,0,-1],[2,0,-2],[1,0,-1]], computes the convolution with weighted kernel correction, and returns the edge-detected image.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `identity_kernel_2` function applies a 3x3 identity convolution to an input image, preserving its content while using memory allocation and cleanup for the kernel. It creates an identity matrix, performs convolution with a correction, and returns the unaltered image.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `cropLft` function crops the left side of an image by `px` pixels using iterative kernel operations. It adjusts `px` to control the crop amount, applies a series of `identity_kernel_3` transformations to progressively modify the image, and returns the cropped result.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `sharpen` function applies a 3x3 convolution kernel to an image to enhance edges, using a sharpening filter (center=100, surrounding=-1) and returns the processed image. It leverages convolution with weighted kernel correction to amplify details while managing intensity scaling.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `brighten` function scales each RGB pixel value of an input image by a given factor `val`, clamping results to valid 0-255 ranges, and returns a new image with the adjusted brightness. It validates input, allocates memory for the output image, and processes each pixel to apply the brightness adjustment.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `convolutionEdgeDetection` function applies a 3x3 Laplacian kernel via convolution to an input image to detect edges, returning the processed image. It uses a weighted kernel correction during convolution and manages memory for the kernel matrix.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `MaxPooling` function performs max pooling on an input image (`IMG`) using a specified kernel, producing a downsampled output image where each pixel represents the maximum grayscale value from the corresponding kernel window. It iterates over the input image with strides defined by the kernel, computes grayscale values, and stores the RGB values of the maximum pixel in each pooling region.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `borderImg` function creates a new image with a border around the input image, using specified RGB colors for the border and copying the original image's pixels inward. It allocates memory for the expanded image, calculates padding for alignment, and fills border pixels while offsetting internal pixels by the border width.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `uncropFilter` function applies a customizable filter to an image after adding a border of thickness `th`, using a provided filter function, and returns the filtered image while freeing temporary memory. It takes an image, a filter function, and a border thickness as inputs.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `pixmap` function creates a new image by applying a given function to each RGB channel of every pixel in the input image, preserving its dimensions and structure while transforming color values. It allocates memory for the new image, calculates row padding for 24-bit alignment, and processes each pixel's RGB components through the provided function.

nodes.title: logmap
nodes.summary: The `logmap` function maps an integer input `p` (typically 0-255) to a compressed logarithmic scale (0-255) by applying a logarithmic transformation, scaling it with `255 / log(256)`, and adding 1 to `p` to avoid log(0) errors.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `histEq` function performs histogram equalization on an input image to enhance contrast by remapping pixel intensities using precomputed lookup tables. It processes each pixel's RGB values through three separate histogram equalization arrays (`hash[0]`, `hash[1]`, `hash[2]`) to generate a new image with equalized intensity distribution.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `erosion_match` function performs morphological erosion on an image using a kernel, producing a new image where each pixel is 255 only if all corresponding kernel positions match specific conditions (255 with kernel 1 or 0 with kernel 0); otherwise, it sets the pixel to 0. Inputs: image and kernel; output: eroded image. Core logic: checks kernel-neighborhood pixel values to determine output pixel values.

nodes.title: gammafunc
nodes.summary: The `gammafunc` function applies gamma correction to an input value `p` (0-255), adjusting it using a gamma exponent to scale brightness in image processing. It computes `(p^gamma / 255^gamma) * 255` to map values nonlinearly.

nodes.title: contraE
nodes.summary: The `contraE` function calculates a value by multiplying the input integer `p` with different constants (`1`, `4`, or `1`) depending on `p`'s range: `1*p` for `p < 10`, `4*p` for `10 ≤ p < 50`, and `1*p` otherwise, returning a `double`.

nodes.title: main
nodes.summary: The `main` function processes an image by applying a 3x3 dilation kernel twice to a black-and-white version, saving the result as "dialation.bmp", while also generating ASCII art of the original image and a black-and-white output. It loads the input image, defines a custom dilation kernel, performs the dilation operation, and saves the processed image.

nodes.title: test2.c
nodes.summary: The 'test2.c' file processes a BMP image using convolution and max pooling operations, then renders the result as dual-format ASCII art in the terminal, managing kernel memory allocation and deallocation throughout the process. It includes functions for applying a 3x3 identity convolution with stride 6 and a 3x3 zero kernel max pooling with stride 3.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary: The `exp_kernel` function applies a 3x3 identity convolution kernel with stride 6 to an input image, returning a processed image, while managing memory allocation and deallocation for the kernel. It uses a weighted kernel correction during convolution.

nodes.title: IMG
nodes.summary:
The `exp_pool` function performs max pooling on an input image using a 3x3 zero matrix kernel, effectively returning a downsampled version of the input with stride 3, while allocating and freeing memory for the kernel.  
**Key actions**: Allocates a zero-filled 3x3 kernel, applies max pooling with stride 3, and returns the result.
